picks.actual: All four legs won: Cook 135 rushing yards (60+); Gibbs 61 receiving yards (25+); Kincaid 7 receptions (4+); LaPorta 6 receptions (4+). Original +360 package wins.
picks.cutoff: All four exact full-game legs at +360 or better. Pass if any threshold rises or the combined price falls below +360. Recheck after 18:30 ET expiry; no automatic renewal.
picks.edge: No demonstrated positive EV and no calibrated joint probability. +360 requires 21.74% to break even; no claim is made that this ticket exceeds that. It returns +3.6u profit and 4.6u total only if every leg wins at the recorded price. Individual historical rates are not multiplied. This is deliberately separate from favorites and their returns.
picks.risk: Kincaid four catches is the weakest historical leg; his five-catch opener does not prove a stable new role. Cook had only 13 carries for 57 yards last week. His two-carry Week 18 rest game stays in the sample. Detroit’s two missing offensive-line starters may reduce route opportunities. All four legs must win; normal workload can still miss one. Official inactives were not yet released/verified at this review.
picks.settlementReason: ESPN summary and scoreboard both explicitly final. All relevant players participated and cleared the original full-game thresholds; no void-leg repricing applies.
picks.title: Four-player volume SGP · full game
picks.why: This exact four-leg package was directly offered in DraftKings’ Indiana experience at +360. The 60-yard Cook and 25-yard Gibbs alternatives are below the researched full-game means; the tight ends need four catches rather than five. At these exact thresholds, last-five/last-ten hits are Cook 3/5 and 6/10, Gibbs 3/5 and 7/10, Kincaid 2/5 and 4/10, LaPorta 4/5 and 7/10. This is an optional speculative fun selection, not a core favorite. Research confidence 6/10 describes verified quote, rules and supporting data, not a 60% chance of winning.

picks.actual: 6 receptions (7 targets, 52 receiving yards); original OVER 4.5 at +116 wins.
picks.cutoff: OVER 4.5 at +100 or better. Pass at 5.5 or any minus price; reverify after quote expiry.
picks.edge: Uncalibrated volume judgment: 6.5 targets times 75% catches gives 4.9 expected receptions, not a probability. Estimated 53% to reach five versus 46.30% break-even at +116: about +6.7 percentage points and +14.5% expected return if that estimate is right. Plausible 47–60% uncertainty and model error are substantial; this is not a calibrated forecast.
picks.risk: His fifth Week 1 catch came in overtime; regulation was four catches for 39 yards. Most historical games precede his 2025 back injury and coordinator change. Missing Detroit linemen could create extra pass-blocking assignments, while St. Brown, Williams and Gibbs compete for targets. Routes remain unverified. This shares Detroit passing-volume exposure with the earlier Gibbs play, so they are not independent parlay legs.
picks.settlementReason: ESPN summary and scoreboard both explicitly final. All relevant players participated and cleared the original full-game thresholds; no void-leg repricing applies.
picks.title: Sam LaPorta OVER 4.5 receptions
picks.why: A plus-money five-catch line fits a conservative 4.9-catch projection. LaPorta has reached five in four of his last five and six of his last ten played games, with last-five targets averaging six. Detroit confirmed his return before Week 1, and Petzing has a documented history of involving tight ends. His eight Week 1 targets support a role, but I trim that to 6.5 rather than extrapolate overtime. Buffalo favored by about 5.5 gives a plausible passing script; no unsupported defensive-funnel boost is applied.

picks.actual: 61 receiving yards (6 receptions, 8 targets); original OVER 29.5 at -115 wins.
picks.cutoff: OVER 29.5 at -115 or better only; pass at 30.5+ or -116 and worse. Reverify the live price after expiry.
picks.edge: Projected mean +3.5 yards, not a probability edge. Uncalibrated judgment: about 55% to clear, versus 53.49% break-even at -115 (about +1.5 percentage points; about +2.8% expected return if that estimate is right). Plausible 50–60% uncertainty includes negative value.
picks.risk: Thin estimated edge and uncertain routes under a new coordinator. Missing Mahogany and Miller could require Gibbs to block instead. Buffalo held Houston RBs to four catches for 17 yards last week; that one game does not prove a favorable matchup. Overtime inflated Week 1 touches. Inactives and wind remain pregame checks; no unsupported weather or scheme boost.
picks.settlementReason: ESPN summary and scoreboard both explicitly final. All relevant players participated and cleared the original full-game thresholds; no void-leg repricing applies.
picks.title: Jahmyr Gibbs OVER 29.5 receiving yards
picks.why: The verified 29.5-yard number is below his 34.4 last-five and 44.9 last-ten averages. Five targets and 30 receiving yards in Week 1 support continuing receiving involvement; the team confirms an expanded lead-back role. My conservative 33-yard projection uses 5.5 targets × 75% catches × 8 yards per catch, below the recent target averages. Buffalo favored by 5.5 gives a plausible passing script. Detroit line absences may encourage outlets, but that is an inference, not the main reason.
